Char: Methods:
RCT, parallel design, 2-armed trial

Review comparisons: early weight-bearing versus delayed weight-bearing; removable ankle support versus non-removable ankle support (after surgical fracture management)
Char: Participants:
Total number of randomised participants: 110

Source population: 2 x level 1 trauma centres (Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre and St. Michael’s Hospital) in Toronto, Canada 

Inclusion criteria: acute unstable unilateral ankle fracture that was considered by the attending staff surgeon to require surgical fixation, including: isolated lateral malleolus fracture with talar shift; vertical shear medial malleolus fractures; bimalleolar fractures; trimalleolar fractures that did not require posterior fragment fixation; closed, grade I, or grade II open fractures

Exclusion criteria: participant-related exclusion factors included: skeletal immaturity, previous ipsilateral ankle surgery, nonambulatory status before injury, inability to comply with postoperative protocol (i.e. advanced dementia), medical comorbidity precluding operative intervention, and people with workers' compensation; people with polytrauma. Fracture-related exclusion factors included: surgical fixation > 14 days from time of injury; grade III open fractures; tibial plafond fractures; syndesmotic injuries/fixation; posterior malleolar fractures requiring fixation. No exclusion criteria with regard to participant age, presence of osteoporosis/osteopenia, or BMI

Baseline characteristics for intervention group

  • Age, mean (SD): 41.7 (± 15.1) years
  • Sex (m/f): 32/24
  • Surgery: all had surgery
  • Fracture severity: unimalleolar: 26; bimalleolar: 25; trimalleolar: 5. OTA: 44A1: 1; 44A2: 2; 44B1: 17; 44B2: 20; 44B3: 11; 44C1: 4; 44C2: 1

Baseline characteristics for control group

  • Age, mean (SD): 42.1 (± 15.4) years
  • Sex (m/f): 27/27
  • Surgery: all had surgery
  • Fracture severity: unimalleolar: 18; bimalleolar: 27; trimalleolar: 9. OTA: 44A1: 1; 44A2: 0; 44B1: 14; 44B2: 27; 44B3: 9; 44C1: 2; 44C2: 1
Char: Interventions:
Timing of randomisation: at the first postoperative visit (2 weeks postoperatively)

Treatment management for both groups: ORIF of unstable ankle fractures with rigid osteosynthesis techniques using standard surgical procedures. Postoperatively, all participants were placed in a below-knee posterior plaster slab and instructed not to bear weight. Posterior slab removed at 2-week visit before randomisation. For boot orthosis, all participants were given a night splint to use in bed while not wearing the orthosis.

Intervention group

  • Number randomised: 56; losses at 6 weeks: 3; at 3 months: 7; at 6 months: 10; at 12 months: 6 (reasons for losses not explained); number analysed at 6 weeks: 53; at 3 months: 49; at 6 months: 56; at 12 months: 50 
  • Treatment management: participants in the early WB group had their ankle placed in a boot orthosis at the 2-week postoperative visit and instructed to start full weight-bearing as tolerated. They were also instructed to remove the orthosis 4 times a day and perform ankle dorsiflexion, plantarflexion, inversion, and eversion exercises. Participants were seen by a physiotherapist, who gave them instructions regarding weight-bearing and range of motion exercises. At the 6-week postoperative visit, participants were instructed to wean from the boot orthosis over the next 2 to 4 weeks.

Control group

  • Number randomised: 54; losses at 3 months: 3; at 6 months: 8; at 12 months: 2 (reasons for losses not explained; number analysed at 6 weeks: 54; at 3 months: 51; at 6 months: 46; at 12 months: 52 
  • Treatment management: participants in the late WB group were placed in a below-knee fibreglass cast at 2 weeks postoperatively and instructed to remain non-weight-bearing for a further 4 weeks (6 weeks total). At the 6-week postoperative visit, the cast was removed, and participants were allowed to perform ankle range of motion exercises and begin full weight-bearing with the use of a boot orthosis. Participants were seen by a physiotherapist, who discussed instructions regarding weight-bearing and range of motion exercises. They were also instructed to wean from the orthosis over the next 2 to 4 weeks.
Char: Outcomes:
Timing of assessment: clinical follow-up at 2 weeks, 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months

End of treatment: 8 to 10 weeks

End of follow-up: 12 months

Included in this review: activity limitation, QoL, adverse events

Other outcomes measured in the study: time to return to work, ankle dorsiflexion range of motion, plantarflexion range of motion

Study dates: 2010 to 2014
